editorial:
Ever wondered why a man who created the world's most logical detective spent his later years chasing ghosts and fairies? You are in for a wild ride with this documentary. It dives deep into the strange life of Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, the guy who gave us Sherlock Holmes. Instead of just listing dates and facts, it feels like a mystery movie where you are uncovering secrets. You get to see how Doyle's obsession with the occult and secret societies actually shaped the characters we love, like the genius Holmes and his evil mirror image, Moriarty. It is a weird, moody look at a man who lived in two different worlds.

What really works here is how the film connects the dots between real history and fiction. The pacing is steady, though some parts feel a bit slow if you just want a quick biography. If you love a good mystery, you will find this fascinating. It is best enjoyed streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best picture, but you could also rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch. If you are a die-hard fan of the detective, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great move so you can rewatch the clues.
endingExplained: The film wraps up by showing that Doyle never stopped believing in the supernatural, even when people laughed at him. It explains that his belief in fairies was not just a mistake, but a way to find meaning in a world that felt too cold and logical. The final scenes show that the tension between science and magic is exactly what made Sherlock Holmes such a great character to begin with.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves Sherlock Holmes or weird history.
